data.title: Branch
data.tagline: Develop an independent line of work without changing the main line
data.description: A branch is a movable name pointing to a series of commits. It lets a feature, fix, or experiment proceed separately and later be merged. Create branches from the right starting point and keep their purpose small enough to review.

use: Fix a bug without disturbing ongoing work
Prepare a release or urgent patch
avoid: Use one long-lived branch for unrelated work
Create it from an outdated or wrong starting point
Keep finished branches forever without a reason
Assume switching branches saves uncommitted changes safely

lessonPractice.title: Main is stable, and you want to try a navigation approach that may be discarded. What is the safer start?

options.label: Stay on main, make the experiment, and decide whether to keep it later
options.feedback: An uncertain large change enters the stable line directly, making experimental work harder to isolate and undo.

options.label: Store current work, then create a purpose-named branch from the latest main
options.feedback: The branch shares the stable starting point while keeping the experiment separate until it is verified.

options.label: Create an entirely new Git repository for the navigation experiment
options.feedback: A new repository disconnects the project's history and collaboration. A branch is the independent line within the same project.

data.agentPrompt: Store current work and sync the latest main, then create a purpose-named branch for the navigation experiment. Change and verify navigation only on that branch, not main. Report the branch, its diff from main, and validation results without merging yet.
